prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your location, roof type, insurance needs, and the company’s experience with hail repairs and claims. I can, however, give you a practical way to find and vet the best roofer for your situation and what to watch out for.

Quick checklist to find the best roofer for hail damage
- Look for experience with hail and storm claims (ask how many hail jobs they do each year).
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, etc.).
- Local presence and history (not a “storm chaser” who disappears after the payout).
- Good online reputation (Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi, Nextdoor) and recent local references.
- Proper insurance and licensing: general liability, workers’ comp, and any local contractor registration required by your city/county.
- Written warranty on workmanship plus manufacturer shingle warranty.
- Clear written estimate with scope, materials, timeline, cleanup, and payment schedule.
- Willingness to work with your insurer and provide photos/documentation—ideally experienced with insurance processes.

Questions to ask any roofer before hiring
- How many hail-repair jobs have you completed in Denver in the last 12 months?
- Can you provide 3 local references (phone numbers) from recent hail repairs?
- Are you a certified installer for major shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ compensation insurance? Can I see certificates?
- Do you handle permits and inspections? Who pulls the permit?
- What is the total written price and what’s included (tear-off, underlayment, flashing, ice & water shield, gutters, cleanup)?
- What warranties do you provide (workmanship length and transferability)?
- Do you require an Assignment of Benefits (AOB)? (Caution: AOBs transfer your claim control — get legal/insurer advice before signing.)

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure “sign today” tactics or unsolicited door-to-door contractors after a storm.
- Requests for very large upfront payments (standard is a modest deposit, not full balance).
- No physical address or poor local track record.
- Asking you to tell the adjuster to write the estimate a certain way, or promising to “guarantee” what the insurance will pay.
- Demands to sign an AOB without explanation.

Working with your insurance company
- Report the claim promptly. Document damage with photos and videos.
- Get at least 2–3 written estimates from reputable roofers.
- Consider an independent roof inspection if you disagree with the insurer’s adjuster.
- Keep receipts and a log of all communications.
- Ask your chosen contractor how they handle supplements if hidden damage is found.

Where to look in Denver
- Check Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and Nextdoor for local recommendations.
- Look for contractors certified by major shingle manufacturers (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed).
- Contact local trade groups (National Roofing Contractors Association or Colorado/local roofing associations) for referrals.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of contractors if you provide your zip code or neighborhood.
- Review 2–3 estimates or company profiles you’re considering and help you compare them.

Tell me your zip code or paste the names of a few contractors you’re deciding between and I’ll help you evaluate them.
